newsitem.title: USA: Leo Burnett Resigns Reebok Account.
newsitem.headline: Leo Burnett Resigns Reebok Account.

text.p: Advertising agency Leo Burnett Co. announced Friday it was quitting its 4-year-old Reebok International Ltd. account, citing a difference in philosophies.

The Chicago-based agency handled the Reebok apparel and footwear lines, and is the only agency working on Reebok's U.S. footwear business. Industry sources have put the Reebok billings at between $40 million and $50 million annually in the United States and another $15 million to $20 million internationally.

"It has become increasingly apparent that our philosophies toward partnership and marketing were out of sync with Reebok's, which was inhibiting us from delivering our best brand-building work," Burnett Chairman Richard Fizdale said in a release.
Leo Burnett has suffered a string of high-profile losses in recent months, including the United Airlines account and the creative portion of Miller Brewing Co.'s Miller Lite business.

Asked why Burnett would resign an account of Reebok's stature in light of recent defections, an agency spokesman said, "The fact that we are resigning the account at this juncture speaks volumes about our relationship (with the client). It shows a commitment about our management to put people and philosophies before the bottom line."
Leo Burnett Co. is the sixth largest advertising agency brand in the world with combined annual billings from domestic and international operations of $5.82 billion in 1996.
